4160:
History After the Lin Biao Incident, the “successor” passage in the Party Constitution of the Ninth Party Congress became void. See Act Four, “How It Happened.”

History The Three Supports and Two Militaries sent out more than two million people in all, and they were withdrawn in stages from 1972. See Yang Jisheng, The World Turned Upside Down (《天地翻覆》), chs. 10 and 13 (paraphrased). By 1972, nearly half of the mass representatives in the leadership of Shanghai's industrial, financial and trade units had been purged. Ibid., ch. 25 (paraphrased).

History At the Ninth Party Congress, Wang Hongwen borrowed 15 yuan from Xu Jingxian to buy a pair of black Dacron trousers. See Li Xun, The Age of Revolutionary Rebellion (《革命造反年代》), ch. 35 (paraphrased). In January 1971 he was elected a secretary of the Shanghai Municipal Party Committee (ranked third). See Wikipedia, “Wang Hongwen.”

Disputed There is no reliable direct record of why Mao Zedong chose Wang Hongwen. The common explanation is that he wanted to train a worker successor.
4163:
In early 1974, Criticize Lin, Criticize Confucius spread across the country. Rebels everywhere treated it as a chance to come back. In Hunan and Hubei, rebels used it to get their posts back and made the unions their base. People who had been purged went to their old work units and took back the materials kept on them. Some burned them on the spot. Large numbers of activists were rushed into the Party and rushed into cadre posts. Tang Zhongfu, a worker in Changsha, came back from a reading class and said he would sharpen the horns on his head.

On January 18, People's Daily printed a letter from Zhong Zhimin, the son of an army cadre. He said he had joined the army and gone to university through the back door, and asked to leave school and go back to the countryside. At the Criticize Lin, Criticize Confucius rally on the 25th, Chi Qun and Xie Jingyi also criticized the back door.

In mid-February, the Chairman wrote to Ye Jianying. He said some who came in through the back door were good people, and some who came in through the front door were bad. Mixing in criticism of the back door might dilute Criticize Lin, Criticize Confucius. On the 20th, on Premier Zhou's suggestion, criticizing the back door was stopped. It was never raised again.
4164:
History During Criticize Lin, Criticize Confucius, rebels in Hunan and Hubei regained their posts, took back and burned materials, and were rushed into the Party and into cadre posts. Tang Zhongfu spoke of sharpening his horns. See Yang Jisheng, The World Turned Upside Down (《天地翻覆》), ch. 25 (paraphrased).

History Zhong Zhimin's request to leave school, the January 25 rally, Mao Zedong's letter to Ye Jianying and the halt on February 20. See Joel Andreas, Rise of the Red Engineers (《红色工程师的崛起》), ch. 8 (paraphrased).
4166:
After Premier Zhou went into the hospital in June, who would run the State Council became the most pressing question. The Fourth National People's Congress was being prepared, and a new leadership had to be settled. The Chairman was not in Beijing at the time. He was staying in Changsha.

The Fengqing was a 10,000-ton oceangoing freighter built by Jiangnan Shipyard and finished at the end of 1973. The Ministry of Transport thought its main engine had problems and wanted it to sail near-sea routes first. Shanghai said this was worshipping foreign things and fawning on foreigners. In 1974 it sailed to Romania, and at the end of September it came back to Shanghai. Shanghai held a huge welcome rally. More than 100,000 people went aboard to look, and the papers called it a powerful criticism of the slavish comprador philosophy.

The Ministry of Transport had sent two cadres on the ship, Li Guotang and Gu Wenguang. They refused to join in criticizing the ministry and the State Council, so they were held in Shanghai and subjected to struggle sessions. The rule was that they could not go back to Beijing until the criticism was thorough. That year, importing equipment and sending people abroad were also called slavish comprador philosophy and crawlism.
4167:
History Zhou Enlai entered the hospital on June 1, 1974. See Wikipedia, “Wang Hongwen” and “Fengqing Incident.” For who would run the State Council after Zhou Enlai entered the hospital, see Act Four, “How It Happened.” Mao Zedong was then at No. 9 Guesthouse in Changsha. See CPC News, “Chronology of the Communist Party of China, 1974.”

History The building of the Fengqing, the dispute between the Ministry of Transport and Shanghai, the voyage to Romania, the publicity on its return to Shanghai, the detention and struggle sessions of Li Guotang and Gu Wenguang, and “no going back to Beijing until the criticism is thorough.” See Wikipedia, “Fengqing Incident,” and the game's glossary entry “Fengqing Incident.”

History Importing equipment and sending people abroad were criticized as “slavish comprador philosophy” and “crawlism.” See the Context panel of Act Four, “$4.3 Billion.”
4170:
In January 1975, after the Fourth National People's Congress, Deng Xiaoping became Vice Chairman of the Central Committee and first Vice Premier of the State Council, in charge of the Central Committee's daily work. The new Constitution wrote in speaking out freely, airing views fully, holding great debates and writing big-character posters.

Deng Xiaoping started with the railways. In March, the Central Committee issued Document No. 9. Wan Li went to the Xuzhou Railway Bureau and arrested the rebel leader Gu Binghua and others. The Xuzhou method was extended to Taiyuan, Zhengzhou and Nanchang. In all, nearly 10,000 people with “serious factionalism” were subjected to struggle sessions, more than 2,000 were arrested and more than 100 were shot. The railways overfulfilled the plan. Later the Ministry of Railways was occupied by petitioners. On the walls it said, if Wan Li doesn't fall, the trains won't run.

Most of the people rectification put down had risen through rebellion. In Hubei, the rebel leaders who had entered the provincial trade union council were sent down on Deng Xiaoping's instructions. A year earlier, during Criticize Lin, Criticize Confucius, people had been rushed into the Party and into cadre posts. The Central Committee issued a document to correct that too.
4171:
History In January 1975 Deng Xiaoping became Vice Chairman and first Vice Premier, in charge of the Central Committee's daily work. See Act Four, “How It Happened.” The 1975 Constitution wrote in the “Four Bigs.” See Wikipedia, “Li Yizhe Incident.”

History Document No. 9, Wan Li's arrest of Gu Binghua in Xuzhou, the extension to Taiyuan, Zhengzhou and Nanchang, nearly 10,000 people struggled, more than 2,000 arrested, more than 100 shot, and “if Wan Li doesn't fall, the trains won't run.” See Yang Jisheng, The World Turned Upside Down (《天地翻覆》), ch. 26 (paraphrased).

History Hubei rebel leaders were sent down on Deng Xiaoping's instructions. Ibid., chs. 11 and 25 (paraphrased). In 1975 the Central Committee issued a document correcting rushed Party admission and promotion. Ibid., ch. 25 (paraphrased).
4174:
In August, the State Planning Commission drafted Some Questions on Accelerating Industrial Development, later called the Twenty Articles on Industry. It told enterprises to rectify their leadership, set up rules and job responsibility, and watch for people doing sabotage in the name of rebellion and going against the tide. In those years the national average pass rate for industrial products was only about 45 percent. In some factories in Tianjin, people actually worked four hours out of eight.

On November 20, the Politburo met. The Chairman wanted a resolution on the Cultural Revolution, with the keynote of seventy percent achievements and thirty percent mistakes, and he wanted Deng Xiaoping in charge of it. The Chairman wanted the veteran cadres and the Cultural Revolution faction to agree on this. Deng Xiaoping declined. He said he was one of the people of the Peach Blossom Spring, who did not know of the Han, let alone the Wei and Jin.

From this month on, the campaign to Counterattack the Right-Deviationist Wind began. Rectification was called reversing verdicts, and Deng Xiaoping was criticized once again.
4175:
History For the content of the Twenty Articles on Industry, see Yang Jisheng, The World Turned Upside Down (《天地翻覆》), ch. 26 (paraphrased). For the pass rate and the Tianjin example, see ibid., ch. 30 (paraphrased).

History On November 20, 1975, Mao Zedong proposed that Deng Xiaoping lead the drafting of a resolution on the Cultural Revolution, with the keynote of seventy percent achievements and thirty percent mistakes. Deng Xiaoping declined as one of the “people of the Peach Blossom Spring.” Mao Zedong hoped the bureaucracy and the Cultural Revolution faction would reach agreement. Ibid., ch. 26 (paraphrased).

History From November 1975 came the campaign to Counterattack the Right-Deviationist Wind, and Deng Xiaoping was criticized again. See Act Four, “How It Happened.”
4177:
From January 1975, Deng Xiaoping ran the daily work of the Central Committee, the State Council and the Central Military Commission. Rectification started with the railways, and most of the people it hit had risen as rebels back then. In history, that year Wang Hongwen was in charge only of the Central study class. He said in private that all the power was Deng Xiaoping's now. The State Council was his, and the army was his too.

On May 3, the Chairman said it once more. Why not unite with the more than 200 Central Committee members. The words were aimed at Jiang Qing and the few others.

In July, in history, Wang Hongwen went back to Shanghai and stayed for several months. Shanghai's militia had grown up after the smashing of the Liansi in 1967. First it was “attack with words, defend with arms” in wicker helmets, and later it was renamed the militia. The army ran less and less of it, and the workers ran more and more of it themselves.
4178:
History In January 1975 Deng Xiaoping became Vice Chairman, first Vice Premier and Chief of the General Staff, in charge of daily work. Wang Hongwen was in charge only of the Central study class. For the Changsha remark “Don't form a gang of four,” see Wikipedia, “Wang Hongwen.” For Wang Hongwen's remark that “all the power is his,” see the game's glossary entry “Deng Xiaoping.”

History For the course and figures of the railway rectification, see Yang Jisheng, The World Turned Upside Down (《天地翻覆》), ch. 26 (paraphrased).

History Mao Zedong on May 3, 1975, “why not unite with the more than 200 Central Committee members.” See Huang Jinhai, Ten Years Not a Dream (《十年非梦》), ch. 11, citing A Brief History of the “Cultural Revolution” (《“文化大革命”简史》).

History Wang Hongwen was back in Shanghai from July to November 1975. See Wikipedia, “Smashing the Shanghai Armed Rebellion Plot.” For the origins of the Shanghai militia, see Li Xun, The Age of Revolutionary Rebellion (《革命造反年代》), ch. 39 (paraphrased).
4180:
From November, the campaign to “Counterattack the Right-Deviationist Wind” began across the country. Deng Xiaoping's rectification that year was said to be an attempt to reverse the verdict on the Cultural Revolution. The same month, in history, Wang Hongwen returned from Shanghai to Beijing.

On January 8, 1976, Premier Zhou died. At the memorial meeting on the 15th, it was still Deng Xiaoping who read the eulogy. When the hearse passed along Chang'an Avenue, the roadside was lined with people. No one had organized them. They came on their own. With the Premier gone, who would run the State Council became the biggest matter in Zhongnanhai.
4181:
History On November 20, 1975, Mao Zedong proposed that Deng Xiaoping lead the drafting of a resolution on the Cultural Revolution, with the keynote of seventy percent achievements and thirty percent mistakes. Deng Xiaoping declined as one of the “people of the Peach Blossom Spring.” See Yang Jisheng, The World Turned Upside Down (《天地翻覆》), ch. 26 (paraphrased). From November 1975 came the “Counterattack the Right-Deviationist Wind.”

History Wang Hongwen was in Shanghai from July to November 1975. See Wikipedia, “Smashing the Shanghai Armed Rebellion Plot.”

History Zhou Enlai died on January 8, 1976. At the memorial meeting on January 15, Deng Xiaoping gave the eulogy. When the hearse passed along Chang'an Avenue, crowds came on their own to see it off.
4184:
On the night of April 5, the square was cleared. Many people were beaten and arrested. The Politburo ruled the events of those Qingming days a counterrevolutionary incident. Outside Beijing, in Nanjing and elsewhere, people also used Qingming to mourn the Premier. They cursed Jiang Qing, Zhang Chunqiao and Yao Wenyuan, and Wang Hongwen too.

On April 7, the Politburo resolved to dismiss Deng Xiaoping from all posts inside and outside the Party. The same month, Hua Guofeng became first Vice Chairman of the Central Committee and Premier of the State Council. The Chairman gave him the post. Jiang Qing and the others were passed over. The campaign to Counterattack the Right-Deviationist Wind went on.

In Shanghai, too, some people took wreaths to People's Square at Qingming, far fewer than in Beijing. In history, during those April Fifth days Wang Hongwen phoned Shanghai and told it to step up combat readiness. The police and the militia jointly drew up a “Plan for Preventing Counterrevolutionary Riots.”
4185:
History On the evening of April 5, militia and police cleared the square. The Politburo ruled it a counterrevolutionary incident. In Beijing, Nanjing and elsewhere, people used Qingming to mourn Zhou Enlai and aimed at Jiang Qing, Zhang Chunqiao, Yao Wenyuan and Wang Hongwen. See the game's glossary entry “Tiananmen Incident” and Wikipedia, “April Fifth Movement.”

History On April 7, 1976, the Politburo resolved to dismiss Deng Xiaoping from all posts inside and outside the Party. In April Hua Guofeng became first Vice Chairman and Premier of the State Council. See Wikipedia, “Wang Hongwen,” and the game's glossary entry “Hua Guofeng.”

History There were also wreaths in Shanghai's People's Square at Qingming, on a much smaller scale than in Beijing. Wang Hongwen told Shanghai to step up combat readiness, and a “Plan for Preventing Counterrevolutionary Riots” was drawn up. See Wikipedia, “Wang Hongwen.”
4188:
On the evening of October 6, Zhang Chunqiao, Wang Hongwen and Yao Wenyuan were detained one after another at Huairen Hall. Jiang Qing and Mao Yuanxin were taken away from where they lived. In one night, everyone on Jiang Qing's side of the Politburo was gone.

Shanghai found out late. From the 8th, the Militia Command set up two command posts, at Jiangnan Shipyard and the China Textile Machinery Plant, and actually gathered about 11,000 people. On the night of the 12th, there was another meeting at Kangping Road. Zhu Yongjia of the writing group said, even if we can't last a week, three days would do. Shi Shangying of the Militia Command refused to move troops. After the meeting he sent orders by telegram that no district militia was to act on its own. He later said his idea was simply to stall. On the afternoon of the 13th, Huang Jinhai told the Party secretary of the No. 31 State Cotton Mill to load the bullets into magazines. The guns and the bullets were still kept apart.

That day, Ma Tianshui, Xu Jingxian and Wang Xiuzhen came back from Beijing to pass on instructions, and the matter was dropped. Not one militiaman went into the streets. A few days later, Shanghai residents marched in the streets on their own to celebrate. The center sent Su Zhenhua, Ni Zhifu and Peng Chong to Shanghai to take charge. Across the country, the investigation of the factional network of the “Gang of Four” began. Ma Tianshui, Xu Jingxian, Wang Xiuzhen and Huang Jinhai were put under isolation and investigation one after another.
4189:
History On the evening of October 6, Zhang Chunqiao, Wang Hongwen and Yao Wenyuan were detained at Huairen Hall, and Jiang Qing and Mao Yuanxin were taken away from where they lived. See the game's Act Five, “How It Happened,” and the glossary entry “Mao Yuanxin.”

History The two command posts from October 8, the roughly 11,000 people actually gathered, the words of Zhu Yongjia and Shi Shangying at the Kangping Road meeting on the night of the 12th, the calling off on the 13th, and the residents' celebration marches. See Li Xun, The Age of Revolutionary Rebellion (《革命造反年代》), ch. 40 (paraphrased). For Huang Jinhai having the bullets loaded into magazines, see Huang Jinhai, Ten Years Not a Dream (《十年非梦》), ch. 11.

Disputed Huang Jinhai records Wang Shaoyong as chairing the meeting on the night of the 12th. Li Xun records Feng Guozhu. This page does not name who chaired it.

History Su Zhenhua, Ni Zhifu and Peng Chong went to Shanghai to take charge. See Wikipedia, “Ni Zhifu” (search summary). For the isolation and investigation of the Shanghai core members, see Huang Jinhai, Ten Years Not a Dream (《十年非梦》), ch. 12.
4191:
On February 7, 1977, a joint editorial of the two papers and one journal said, whatever policy decisions Chairman Mao made, we will resolutely uphold, and whatever instructions Chairman Mao gave, we will always follow. Later people called this the “Two Whatevers.” By this logic, nothing the Chairman had decided could be changed.

In July, the Third Plenum of the Tenth Central Committee restored Deng Xiaoping's posts. The same plenum expelled you from the Party. In August the Eleventh Party Congress met. Hua Guofeng became Chairman, and Ye Jianying, Deng Xiaoping, Li Xiannian and Wang Dongxing became Vice Chairmen. Hua Guofeng's side and Deng Xiaoping's side sat at one table, and their differences kept growing.

On May 11, 1978, Guangming Daily ran a special commentator's article, “Practice is the sole criterion of truth.” The next day the two papers reprinted it. Wang Dongxing and others criticized the article. On June 2, Deng Xiaoping spoke on seeking truth from facts at the All-Army Political Work Conference. The “Two Whatevers” could no longer stand. In November, the Beijing Municipal Party Committee announced that the Tiananmen Incident was entirely a revolutionary action.

From November 10, the Central Work Conference met, and it went on until December 15. At the meeting Chen Yun raised old questions, such as the Sixty-One Renegades case, Peng Dehuai and the Tiananmen Incident. Some in the hall applauded.
4192:
History The “Two Whatevers” come from the joint editorial of the two papers and one journal on February 7, 1977. In July 1977 the Third Plenum of the Tenth Central Committee restored Deng Xiaoping's posts and expelled Wang Hongwen from the Party. In August the Eleventh Party Congress elected the Chairman and Vice Chairmen.

History The special commentator's article in Guangming Daily on May 11, 1978, was reprinted by the two papers the next day. Wang Dongxing and others criticized it. Deng Xiaoping spoke on seeking truth from facts at the All-Army Political Work Conference on June 2. In November 1978 the Beijing Municipal Party Committee announced that the Tiananmen Incident was “entirely a revolutionary action.”

History The Central Work Conference ran from November 10 to December 15, 1978. Chen Yun's speech raised the Sixty-One Renegades case, Peng Dehuai, the Tiananmen Incident and other questions. See the game's character entry “Chen Yun.”
4195:
After the Third Plenum, cases decided in the past were overturned one by one. In 1979, Shadian was rehabilitated and no longer counted as a counterrevolutionary armed rebellion. The three behind Li Yizhe, who had put up big-character posters in Guangzhou and were arrested in 1977, were also rehabilitated that year.

In February 1980, at the Fifth Plenum of the Eleventh Central Committee, Wang Dongxing, Ji Dengkui, Wu De and Chen Xilian resigned their posts. That year, the National People's Congress decided to delete “speaking out freely, airing views fully, holding great debates, writing big-character posters” from the Constitution. When it was written into the Constitution in 1975, Wang Hongwen was Vice Chairman.

On November 20, the Special Court of the Supreme People's Court opened to try the ten principal defendants of the “Lin Biao and Jiang Qing counterrevolutionary cliques.” The charges against Wang Hongwen included Kangping Road, the Shanghai Diesel Liansi, the 1968 pamphlet that framed Chen Yi, and the Shanghai militia. Anting was not among them.
4196:
History The Shadian Incident was rehabilitated in 1979. See Wikipedia, “Shadian Incident.” The three behind Li Yizhe were arrested in 1977 and rehabilitated in 1979. See Wikipedia, “Li Yizhe Incident.”

History At the Fifth Plenum of the Eleventh Central Committee in February 1980, Wang Dongxing, Ji Dengkui, Wu De and Chen Xilian resigned. See the game's Act Six, “How It Happened.” In 1980 the National People's Congress deleted the “Four Bigs” from the Constitution. See the game's glossary entry “Four Bigs.”

History The Special Court opened on November 20, 1980, to try ten principal defendants. The charges against Wang Hongwen included Kangping Road, the Shanghai Diesel Liansi, Collection of Chen Yi's Reactionary Remarks (《陈毅反动言论小集》) and Shanghai's “second armed force.” The Anting Incident was not among them. See the game's glossary entry “Special Court” and Wikipedia, “Wang Hongwen.”
4199:
Beijing had finished its trial, but the Shanghai cases had not been heard yet. Ma Tianshui, Xu Jingxian, Wang Xiuzhen, Huang Jinhai and others had been under isolation and investigation since October 1976. The Maqiao barracks was one of the places they were held, for years on end. Ma Tianshui had a mental breakdown during the investigation.

From July to August 1982, the Shanghai Higher and Intermediate People's Courts tried the core members of the “Gang of Four” in Shanghai. On August 21, Wang Xiuzhen was sentenced to 17 years in prison. Xu Jingxian got 18 years, Huang Jinhai 15, and Zhu Yongjia of the writing group 14. Some of those who had made preparations in the militia during that week in October 1976 were also sentenced for “plotting armed rebellion.”

During the investigation, the special case group also asked them about Wang Hongwen. Xu Jingxian testified that on the day of Kangping Road, Zhang Chunqiao had told Wang Hongwen to send people to fight. Huang Jinhai told the special case group that Wang Hongwen was with him when it happened and did not know what was going on at Kangping Road.
4200:
History From July to August 1982, the Shanghai higher and intermediate courts tried the core members of the “Gang of Four” in Shanghai, and Huang Jinhai was sentenced to 15 years. The Maqiao barracks was one of the places of isolation and investigation. See Huang Jinhai, Ten Years Not a Dream (《十年非梦》), ch. 12.

History On August 21, 1982, Wang Xiuzhen was sentenced to 17 years, Xu Jingxian to 18 and Zhu Yongjia to 14. Ma Tianshui had a mental breakdown during isolation and investigation. See the game's glossary entries “Wang Xiuzhen,” “Xu Jingxian,” “Zhu Yongjia” and “Ma Tianshui.” Militia participants were sentenced for “plotting armed rebellion.” See the source notes for Act Five.

Disputed Xu Jingxian testified to an instruction about Kangping Road. Huang Jinhai said Wang Hongwen was with him at the time. The two accounts differ. Huang Jinhai later found a different record in his own work notebook. See Huang Jinhai, Ten Years Not a Dream (《十年非梦》), ch. 12.

Dream and Not DreamShanghai　Beijing　1966 to 1978

Qincheng Prison, a night sometime in the 1980s. The corridor light stays on all night.

You dream of that winter again. The smoke-filled room on Yuyuan Road, the tens of thousands of people at Culture Square, the two cold rails at Anting Station, the armbands all over the ground on Kangping Road.

Things in the dream can go differently. When you wake, the dossier is still the same dossier.

The game remembers what you did and how others remember you. It also keeps four values, Sharing Power, Leniency, Clean Hands and Favor. Every choice adds to them or takes away from them, and you can click a value's name to see what it means. In every section you can open “Source notes” to see what is history, what is disputed and what is fiction. There are six acts, ending in December 1978. A playthrough is long, and you can pick up the last dream from the title page at any time. At the end of each playthrough, the ending page gives a world line code that records how this playthrough changed the world.
